case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven.** It's my pick, rated 2 (average) for boats this week.
- Fish 40-100 ft of water, and run lines about 45-100 ft down, where past reports found the salmon.
- Start with glow or chrome J-plugs and meat rigs. Glow spoons and white flies also got bites.
- My ratings for boat fishing this week: Grand Haven 2, Muskegon 1, South Haven 1, St. Joseph 1 (low confidence).

## Why
- **Grand Haven has the most recent good boat report.** The Aug 30 Grand Haven report rated boats good (3) in 40-80 ft of water, while the other three ports' latest boat reports were slow or unrated.
- **Muskegon and South Haven were slow last week.** Both had slow boat reports on Aug 30, and Muskegon's was also slow on Aug 23.
- **The water warmed this week, which I'd expect to slow the bite.** The buoy rose 12 F over the week, so the sharp drop that brought fish in on Aug 30 seems to have reversed.
- **St. Joseph has too little data.** Its only boat report was unrated and mostly had no fishing at all because of poor weather.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is Aug 30, six days old)
- Grand Haven, Aug 30: boats "reported salmon action as good in 40 to 80 feet of water"; "Glow or chrome J-plugs worked well, along with white flasher/flies." Rated 3 (good).
- Grand Haven, Aug 23: boats "trolling around the pierheads found the salmon action to be slow"; best fish were "45 to 100 down in 90 to180 feet of water." Rated 0.
- Muskegon, Aug 30: "Boat anglers found the action to be slow"; best fishing was "55 to 100 feet in 70 to 130 feet of water." Rated 0.
- South Haven, Aug 30: "When boat anglers made it out, the salmon fishing was pretty good," with the best fish "around 100 feet," but the report was rated 0. Meat rigs, rotators and flies caught the most fish.
- St. Joseph, Aug 30: "Due to poor weather, very few anglers made it out"; boats targeted "90 to 100 feet of water." Not rated.

**Past seasons** (general history, not this year's reports)
- At similar surface temperatures (about 66 F), Grand Haven boats were rated good on Aug 30 (2023) and Aug 16 (2023), both in weeks with a sharp temperature drop. Grand Haven boats were slow on Aug 23 (2023), a week with no drop.
- In 2022, similar weeks were mostly average or below for boats at all four ports.

**Conditions now**
- The buoy data is a summary of the week before Sept 5: surface water averaged 63 F at the Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy (+12 F over the week), 68 F at South Haven (+5 F), and 71 F at St. Joseph (+4 F).
- Grand Haven and Muskegon share the same buoy, so their water readings are identical.
- I have no current wind forecast or modeled cold-layer depth in this data.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and the tool returned a summary for the week before Sept 5, not live data. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- Only one boat report per port this week; St. Joseph has essentially none.
- I have no wind forecast here. Check it before you go; for a small boat, strong wind or big waves mean the pier or river is the safer choice.
- General guidance (not from a report): Chinook and coho usually hold in water of 52-58 F. Since the buoy is warming, the fish may sit deeper than the reports describe.

## Sources
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Aug 30 DNR bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/36d9d5d
- Grand Haven, Aug 23 DNR bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/36c669b
- Grand Haven, Aug 16 DNR bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/36b27d5
